definition: The specific group of people a product or message is made for.
business_context_example: Our target audience is HR managers in companies with 50 to 200 employees.

definition: How well people know and recognize a brand.
business_context_example: The podcast didn't sell anything directly, but it built brand awareness.

definition: The words that tell people exactly what to do next, like 'Sign up' or 'Book now'.
business_context_example: The email had no call to action, so nobody knew what to click.

definition: The percentage of visitors who do what you want, like buying or signing up.
business_context_example: The new page design lifted our conversion rate from 2% to 5%.

definition: The percentage of people who click a link after seeing it.
business_context_example: The second subject line doubled our click-through rate.

definition: A single web page made for one goal, usually collecting sign-ups or sales.
business_context_example: We sent the ad traffic to a landing page, not to the homepage.

definition: A free gift, like a guide or checklist, offered in exchange for an email address.
business_context_example: Our lead magnet is a free PDF with 20 email templates in English.

definition: The steps a person goes through from first hearing about you to buying.
business_context_example: People enter our sales funnel through the free webinar.

definition: The process of finding people who might become customers.
business_context_example: LinkedIn posts are our cheapest channel for lead generation.

definition: How much people react to your content: likes, comments, shares, replies.
business_context_example: Question posts get 3 times more engagement than photos.

definition: The number of different people who see your content.
business_context_example: The reel had a reach of 12,000, mostly people who don't follow us.

definition: The total number of times your content was shown, including repeats.
business_context_example: The ad got 50,000 impressions but only 90 clicks.

definition: Visitors who find you without paid ads, usually through search or social media.
business_context_example: The blog brings steady organic traffic, about 800 visits a month.

definition: Advertising you pay for, like Facebook or Google ads.
business_context_example: We spend 200 euro a month on paid ads and track every lead.

definition: Comparing two versions of something to see which works better.
business_context_example: A/B testing showed that the shorter headline sold more.

definition: Writing text whose job is to sell or persuade.
business_context_example: Good copywriting turned the boring course page into our best seller.

definition: The title of an ad, page, or article; the first line people read.
business_context_example: Test 5 headlines before you spend money on the ad.

definition: A short, memorable phrase connected to a brand.
business_context_example: Their tagline is 3 words long and everyone remembers it.

definition: The one thing that makes your offer different from competitors.
business_context_example: Our unique selling point is lessons built around the client's real work emails.

definition: A clear statement of what the customer gets and why it's worth it.
business_context_example: The value proposition on the homepage answers 'why us' in one sentence.

definition: A small, specific part of a market.
business_context_example: We picked a niche: English for finance teams, not English for everyone.

definition: How you want customers to see your brand compared to others.
business_context_example: Our positioning is premium: fewer clients, deeper work, higher price.

definition: The planned introduction of a new product to the market.
business_context_example: The product launch starts with a 3-email warm-up sequence.

definition: Releasing something quietly to a small group before the big public launch.
business_context_example: We did a soft launch with 10 loyal clients to catch problems early.

definition: To make people talk about something before or during a launch.
business_context_example: The countdown posts created buzz a week before the course opened.

definition: To spread very quickly online because people keep sharing it.
business_context_example: Her 15-second office joke went viral and brought 2,000 followers.

definition: A person with an online audience who can affect what people buy.
business_context_example: A local influencer mentioned our cafe and the weekend was full.

definition: A customer's statement saying they liked your product or service.
business_context_example: We added 3 testimonials under the price and sales went up.

definition: A detailed story of how a real customer got results with your product.
business_context_example: The case study shows how a hotel team improved their email English in 8 weeks.

definition: A new customer sent to you by an existing customer.
business_context_example: Half of our students come from referrals, so we thank every one.

definition: Keeping existing customers instead of losing them.
business_context_example: Customer retention is cheaper than winning new clients with ads.

definition: The rate at which customers stop buying or cancel.
business_context_example: Churn goes up every summer, so we plan a July offer.

definition: To offer a customer a bigger or better version of what they're buying.
business_context_example: After the group course, we upsell private lessons to the most active students.

definition: To offer a customer a related product in addition to what they're buying.
business_context_example: The bookshop cross-sells notebooks and pens at the counter.

definition: A period when people can use a product without paying.
business_context_example: The 7-day free trial converts about 1 in 5 users into subscribers.

definition: A special lower price for people who buy before everyone else.
business_context_example: The early bird price ends Sunday, then it goes up by 30%.

definition: A list of people who want to buy when a product becomes available.
business_context_example: The course is full, but the waiting list already has 40 names.

definition: The percentage of people who open an email you sent.
business_context_example: Emails with a question in the subject line get a higher open rate.

definition: To choose to stop receiving someone's emails.
business_context_example: A few people unsubscribe after every sales email, and that's normal.

definition: A regular email sent to a list of subscribers with news or useful content.
business_context_example: The weekly newsletter goes out every Tuesday at 9 am.

definition: A plan showing what content you will publish and when.
business_context_example: The content calendar has 3 posts a week planned a month ahead.

definition: Content that stays useful for years, not just this week.
business_context_example: The grammar guides are evergreen content, they bring readers all year.

definition: The personality and style a brand uses in all its communication.
business_context_example: Our brand voice is warm and direct, never corporate and cold.

definition: Using stories instead of dry facts to connect with an audience.
business_context_example: Storytelling works: the post about one student's job interview beat every ad.

definition: A specific problem your customer has that your product solves.
business_context_example: The biggest pain point for our clients is writing emails to foreign partners.

definition: Evidence that other people trust you: reviews, numbers, logos, testimonials.
business_context_example: Adding 'trusted by 300 students' gave the page instant social proof.

definition: Collecting information about customers and competitors before you act.
business_context_example: Two weeks of market research saved us from building the wrong course.

definition: All the steps and contacts a customer has with your brand over time.
business_context_example: We mapped the customer journey from first Instagram visit to signed contract.

definition: How much profit you get compared to what you spent.
business_context_example: The ads cost 500 euro and brought 4 clients, a clear return on investment.

definition: A contest where people can win a free product, usually for likes, shares, or emails.
business_context_example: The giveaway added 900 followers, but only a few became clients.
